title: Homotopy independence of quotient tensor resolution lifts
statement: Let $A,C$ be commutative rings, $I\subseteq A$ and $J\subseteq C$ ideals, and $\varphi:A\to C$ a ring homomorphism. Let $P\to A/I$ and $R\to C/J$ be projective resolutions, meaning nonnegative chain complexes of projective modules with quasi-isomorphic augmentations [def-weil-pbc-projective-module, def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. Let $\psi:A/I\to C/J$ commute with the quotient maps and $\varphi$. Suppose $a,a':P\to\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}R$ are chain maps with $\pi_Ra_0=\psi\pi_P=\pi_Ra'_0$. Suppose $k,k':P\otimes_A(A/I)\to\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}(R\otimes_C(C/J))$ are chain maps satisfying $k_j(x\otimes y)=a_j(x)\otimes\psi(y)$ and $k'_j(x\otimes y)=a'_j(x)\otimes\psi(y)$. Then there is a chain homotopy between $k$ and $k'$. No flatness of $C$ over $A$ or projectivity of restricted $R_j$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 00LS(2), lemma-compare-resolutions: induction by lifting through differentials, applied to projectives and then quotient tensoring

proof.text: Restrict the augmented R-complex along the exact additive restriction-of-scalars functor. The exact short complexes at degree zero and every positive degree remain exact. The common augmentation equations make (a-a')_0 vanish after the restricted augmentation. Exactness here has its kernel-image meaning [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence].

Use the upstream theorem's private augmented lifting induction: subtract a_prime from a, lift the degree-zero residual through the augmentation kernel, and inductively lift each residual through the next differential using exactness and source projectivity. Homotopy.mkInductive and Homotopy.equivSubZero assemble a homotopy between a and a_prime; target projectivity is never used. This is the same complete proof as before retirement, now read in the upstream module.

For each component H_j define the semilinear tensor map H_j tensor psi by TensorProduct.map and view it as A-linear into restriction of scalars. Quotient compatibility proves that psi is varphi-semilinear. The component vanishes when H_j does. Evaluate the differential identity on pure tensors, use the two equations for k and k', and distribute tensor over the sum in H.comm. TensorProduct.ext proves the full homotopy identity. All these steps are implemented in Lean with no remaining hole.

lean.statement:
theorem quotient_tensor_resolution_lift_homotopy
    {A C : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing C]
    (I : Ideal A) (J : Ideal C) (φ : A →+* C)
    (P : ProjectiveResolution (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ I)))
    (R : ProjectiveResolution (ModuleCat.of C (C ⧸ J))) :
    let TA := (tensorRight (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ I))).mapHomologicalComplex (.down ℕ)
    let TC := (tensorRight (ModuleCat.of C (C ⧸ J))).mapHomologicalComplex (.down ℕ)
    ∀ (ψ : (A ⧸ I) →+* (C ⧸ J))
      (a a' : P.complex ⟶ ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars φ).mapHomologicalComplex
        (.down ℕ)).obj R.complex)
      (k k' : TA.obj P.complex ⟶ ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars φ).mapHomologicalComplex
        (.down ℕ)).obj (TC.obj R.complex)),
      (∀ x : A, ψ (Ideal.Quotient.mk I x) = Ideal.Quotient.mk J (φ x)) →
      (∀ x : P.complex.X 0, R.π.f 0 (a.f 0 x) = ψ (P.π.f 0 x)) →
      (∀ x : P.complex.X 0, R.π.f 0 (a'.f 0 x) = ψ (P.π.f 0 x)) →
      (∀ (j : ℕ) (x : P.complex.X j) (y : A ⧸ I),
        k.f j (x ⊗ₜ[A] y) = (show R.complex.X j from a.f j x) ⊗ₜ[C] (ψ y)) →
      (∀ (j : ℕ) (x : P.complex.X j) (y : A ⧸ I),
        k'.f j (x ⊗ₜ[A] y) = (show R.complex.X j from a'.f j x) ⊗ₜ[C] (ψ y)) →
      Nonempty (Homotopy k k')
